title: The toolchain audit flags a pin whose mise install does not provide the command the project calls
body:
Observed 2026-11-19: five repositories pinned `"github:composer/composer" = "2.x"`; the github backend installs the release asset as `composer.phar`, so the pin provides no `composer` command and every `composer` call (mise tasks, gates) silently fell through to the system package `/usr/bin/composer` 2.10.3. The toolchain audit reported the repositories as current. Fix on the host: `{ version = "2.11.2", bin = "composer" }`.
Principle: a pinned tool must provide the command the project calls under its pinned name; a pin that resolves elsewhere is a hidden second version.
Files: scripts/toolchain-audit.ts, test/ (audit test), .agents/skills/workstation/SKILL.md
Outcome: the audit prints a `provides` line for every pinned tool whose short name (backend prefix and owner stripped; `composer` for `github:composer/composer`) has no executable in that version's mise install while a same-named command exists elsewhere on PATH, naming the config and the fix (`bin = "<name>"` for github/aqua/http backends); the workstation skill states the principle in one line with the composer table form as the example.
Proof: an audit test with a fixture install dir holding only `composer.phar` prints the `provides` line, and one holding `composer` prints none.
